newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia introduces first Internet service.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia introduces first Internet service.

text.p: Ethiopia has introduced its first domestic connection to the Internet with a capacity of 5,000 clients, the head of the state-owned service said on Friday.

Fanata Adane of the Ethiopian Internet Bureau, owned by the Ethiopian Telecommunications Authority, said government bodies would be charged $75 for registration and $50 for 30 hours of service a month.
Non-governmental organisations pay $150 registration and $100 for each 30 hours access per month while individuals would pay $75 and $25 respectively for the same service, he said.
Additional hours are available beyond 30 at $3 per hour.
Previously access to the Internet was only available from Ethiopia through costly calls to a service provider abroad.
